# 03 ΓÇö Manuscript diagnosis (Stage 30)

Prepared by: Claude Code, stage `30_manuscript`, requested model Fable 5 /
Extra High. Audited artifact: the submitted IEEE Sensors Letters manuscript
`SENSL-26-07-RL-1061` ("AlGaN/GaN Hall-Effect Sensor for In-Situ Magnetic
Field Monitoring of the HSX Stellarator"), read from its LaTeX source
[`../../01_Publications/submitted/regular_lsens/regular_lsens.tex`](../../01_Publications/submitted/regular_lsens/regular_lsens.tex)
(line numbers below refer to that file; per
[`00_INPUT_INVENTORY.md`](00_INPUT_INVENTORY.md) Group B the source compiles
to the identical PDF contained in
[`../inputs/IEEE_submission_bundle_2026-07-02.pdf`](../inputs/IEEE_submission_bundle_2026-07-02.pdf),
whose embedded viewer restrictions prevented direct PDF re-extraction in this
stage). Reviewer wording is from
[`../inputs/Decision_Letter_IEEE_2026-07-23.pdf`](../inputs/Decision_Letter_IEEE_2026-07-23.pdf)
(read in full this stage). Claim IDs `C###` refer to
[`00_CLAIM_BASELINE.csv`](00_CLAIM_BASELINE.csv); conflict IDs to
[`00_CONFLICT_LEDGER.md`](00_CONFLICT_LEDGER.md); source IDs `S####` to
[`01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv`](01_SOURCE_LEDGER.csv). Reviewer-comment IDs
(`AE-##`, `R1-##`, `R2-##`) refer to
[`03_REVIEWER_RESPONSE_MATRIX.csv`](03_REVIEWER_RESPONSE_MATRIX.csv).

Evidence-category legend used throughout: **[SF]** supplied fact,
**[EE]** external evidence (verified ledger source or official policy),
**[INF]** inference, **[REC]** recommendation, **[PX]** proposed experiment
(handed to stage 40), **[GATE]** unresolved gate.

This stage diagnoses only. **No manuscript file was edited.**

---

## 1. Claim-by-claim audit

### 1.1 Title (line 370)

| Claim | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| "AlGaN/GaN Hall-Effect Sensor" | **Supported now** | Device identity is a supplied fact (C001) [SF] |
| "for In-Situ ΓÇª Monitoring of the HSX Stellarator" | **Supported now** (deployment happened; C001) | [SF] |
| "Magnetic Field Monitoring" | **Requires qualification today; fully supported only after calibration** | The delivered output is voltage-domain only; no tesla value exists anywhere in the study or data (C005; `00_INPUT_INVENTORY.md` Group C). The AE's core objection (AE-01) is precisely this gap between the title's measurand and the reported quantity. [SF]/[INF] |

**[REC]** Keep the title only if the revision delivers field-unit output
(WP-C); otherwise it over-promises the measurand.

### 1.2 Abstract (active 150-word version, lines 426ΓÇô429)

| # | Claim (abridged) | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Direct sensors address integration drift in inductive fusion diagnostics | **Supported now** | Field-standard motivation; manuscript refs ref3/ref4; independently corroborated by [S0068](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/ac8aad), [S0114](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5038871) [EE] |
| A2 | HSX is "the first quasi-helically symmetric stellarator" | **Requires qualification (wording)** | Peer-reviewed support exists but with more precise wording: [S0128](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6587/adb179) calls HSX the "first and only stellarator experiment optimized for quasi-helical symmetry"; exact quasi-helical symmetry is impossible in principle [S0124](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.859916). Stage-10B/10D gate: match S0128's wording, do not paraphrase loosely. [EE] |
| A3 | 1 T on-axis field; up to 200 kW launched ECRH | **Supported now** (cited facility parameters, refs 13/14) | [SF]/[EE]; not re-derived here |
| A4 | Sensor fabricated, packaged, deployed in-vessel near plasma edge | **Supported now** (C001) | [SF] |
| A5 | "During 68 consecutive plasma discharge shots, the sensor remained functional" | **Requires qualification** | C002: the supplied archive documents shots 9ΓÇô68 (60 distinct documented shots, including non-plasma coil-only shots such as shot 68 itself); the literal count "68 consecutive **plasma** discharge shots" was not reproduced from `test_note.docx` in any stage. A recount is a supplied-data analysis (┬º4.1). [SF]/[INF] |
| A6 | Clear transient responses associated with ignition and discharge dynamics | **Supported now** (raw traces in archive) | [SF] |
| A7 | Biased/unbiased and plasma/coil-only comparisons confirm Hall origin | **Supported now** (Fig. 4 logic; data present) | [SF] |
| A8 | Temporal correlation with diamagnetic-loop stored energy across three discharge classes | **Supported now, qualitatively** ΓÇö currently uncorroborated by any correlation statistic; quantifiable from supplied data (┬º4.1) | [SF]/[INF] |

### 1.3 Introduction (lines 448ΓÇô453)

| # | Claim | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | Fusion/ML motivation (refs Ongena2016, Degrave2022, Anirudh2023) | Supported now (citations) | [EE] |
| I2 | Integrator drift mechanism in Mirnov-type diagnostics (refs 3ΓÇô4) | Supported now | [EE]; note R1-03: the Mirnov sentence should re-cite ref2 (Endler W7-X = [S0131](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fusengdes.2015.07.020)) |
| I3 | "conventional Hall-effect devices based on silicon, GaAs, InAs, InSb **cannot be deployed near the plasma edge**" | **Requires qualification** | Over-general as written: non-GaN Hall systems are deployed long-term in fusion devices ΓÇö JET's InSb probe system operated 11+ years [S0068], ITER's steady-state set uses bismuth Hall sensors [S0113](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4732077)ΓÇô[S0115](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5038812), plus CASTOR [S0070](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10582-006-0185-4)/[S0117](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2971209), EAST [S0069](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fusengdes.2008.07.045). The defensible statement is about *temperature/radiation headroom limits* of narrow-gap III-V near the plasma edge, cited as prior art, not a blanket impossibility. This rewrite is also the correct answer to R2-01. [EE]/[REC] |
| I4 | 2DEG physics and high mobility (refs 9ΓÇô10) | Supported now | [EE] |
| I5 | AlGaN/GaN sensitivity stable to 576 ┬░C (ref11 = [S0006](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5139911)) | Supported now (as citation of prior group work) | [EE] |
| I6 | "we demonstrate ΓÇª in-situ magnetic field monitoring ΓÇª with a 1 MHz readout bandwidth across 68 consecutive shots" | **Requires qualification + new evidence** | Bundles three exposures: the measurand gap (AE-01), the underived 1 MHz figure (C003, R1-04/AE-07), and the shot-count wording (A5). [SF]/[INF] |
| I7 | Novelty framing (implicit: first such demonstration) | **Requires reframing** | The manuscript never states its "first" precisely, which let R2 attack device-granularity novelty. Defensible granularity (Stage 20 ┬º5): first GaN/WBG 2DEG Hall sensor operated in-vessel in any magnetic-confinement device; first Hall sensor of any kind in a QHS stellarator ΓÇö both bounded absence findings from the 231-source ledger, with the non-GaN fusion Hall lineage cited as prior art. "First fusion Hall diagnostic" is false and must never appear. [EE]/[REC] |

### 1.4 Methods (Section II, lines 455ΓÇô487)

| # | Claim | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Wafer stack, fabrication process, octagonal plate (200 ┬╡m), 5├ù5 mm die (lines 457, Fig. 1) | Supported now (supplied facts; process consistent with cited group lineage ref10/ref11) | [SF] |
| M2 | Packaging: LCC, Al wire bonds, EPO-TEK 353ND, 150 ┬░C vacuum bake, zirconia holder, graphite shield (line 465) | Supported now | [SF] |
| M3 | Bias from oscilloscope waveform generator (Keysight DSOX1204G); INA849 + 2├ùOPA814 chain (line 483) | Supported now | [SF]; consistent with project 02 `SPECS.md` (C004) |
| M4 | Total gain 200 V/V (line 483) | Supported now (C004, cross-consistent with SPECS.md) ΓÇö not independently re-measured | [SF] |
| M5 | Bandwidth 1 MHz (line 483) | **Requires new evidence** | C003 `disputed_by_reviewer`; no derivation exists in the manuscript, its references, or `SPECS.md` (AE-07/R1-04). [SF] |
| M6 | Equations (1)ΓÇô(2): V_H = S_v┬╖V_bias┬╖B; V_out = A_v┬╖V_H + V_off (C023) | Supported now | [SF] |
| M7 | V_off bias-independent, temperature-dependent (ref15 Dowling dissertation) | Supported now as cited claim | [EE] (dissertation ΓÇö not a peer-reviewed ledger source; acceptable as a citation, not counted toward the ledger) |
| M8 | Biased-vs-unbiased comparison isolates Hall response from offset/EMI/charge artifacts | Supported now (methodologically sound; Fig. 4 data exists) ΓÇö strengthenable via the bias-scaling analysis in ┬º4.1 | [SF]/[INF] |
| M9 | "Absolute calibration of V_off ΓÇª remain future work" (line 487) | Supported now ΓÇö the manuscript's own honest limitation (C005) | [SF] |

### 1.5 Results (Section III, lines 494ΓÇô504)

| # | Claim | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-1 | Shot sequence description (motor generators, 48 coils, ~800 ms ramp, 50 ms flat-top, 28 GHz ECRH) | Supported now (facility description, refs 13/14/16) | [SF]/[EE] |
| R-2 | Fig. 4(a) unbiased (63) vs biased (65); Fig. 4(b) plasma (65) vs coil-only (68) behavior | Supported now ΓÇö shots 63/65/68 have corresponding raw files in the archive (`00_CONFLICT_LEDGER.md` non-conflict list) | [SF] |
| R-3 | "Across the 68 discharge shots, the shape and timing of this transient repeated reliably under comparable conditions, indicating stable sensor operation" (line 496) | **Requires qualification as written; upgradeable by analysis** | Currently a qualitative assertion with no statistic. A per-shot transient amplitude/timing distribution is computable from the 73 supplied scope files (┬º4.1) and would convert this into a defensible operational-repeatability claim (distinct from AE-03's *fabrication* repeatability, which needs new bench data). [SF]/[INF] |
| R-4 | Diamagnetic-loop comparison across three discharge classes; ~30 ms DAQ offset (line 504) | Supported now qualitatively; correlation statistic recoverable (┬º4.1) | [SF] |
| R-5 | "establishes that the ΓÇª sensor can track plasma-dependent magnetic-field dynamics in real time" (line 504) | **Requires qualification** | True in the voltage/temporal domain only; "magnetic-field dynamics" in field units is exactly what is not yet delivered (AE-01). [INF] |

### 1.6 Figures

| Figure | Audit result |
|---|---|
| Fig. 1 (die schematic/optical) | No issues raised; supported. |
| Fig. 2 (packaging/in-vessel) | Supported; becomes more valuable if AE-08's system framing is adopted. |
| Fig. 3 (readout chain) | Supported; a revision should annotate the bandwidth-limiting element once AE-07/R1-04 is answered. |
| Fig. 4 (functional verification) | Supported by archive data (shots 63/65/68). |
| Fig. 5 (stored energy vs sensor output; shots 21/18/19) | Data supported ([SF]; shots 18ΓÇô21 `.dat` files and the 73 scope CSVs re-verified present this stage; the per-shot scope-file mapping rests on Stage 00's `test_note.docx` audit); **presentation fails AE-05** (volts, not field units) and R1-05 suggests an overlay format. Conversion requires WP-C. |

### 1.7 Conclusion (line 506)

Restates A4ΓÇôA8 (same statuses apply). Two additional findings:

1. **Future-work sentence partially conflicts with the mission scope rule
   [SF vs SF conflict]:** it promises "radiation and neutron irradiation
   characterization at a dedicated facility." The parent scope rule and
   MISSION.md state **no neutron/gamma experiments are planned** in Tim's
   experimental work; radiation belongs to the co-authored simulation-only
   TCAD paper (C024). **[REC]** In any revision, replace with: radiation
   response addressed via complementary TCAD modeling (co-authored, in
   preparation) and literature ([S0002](https://doi.org/10.1109/TMAG.2012.2196986),
   [S0054](https://doi.org/10.1149/2.0251602jss)), cited as outlook only. Promising an experiment that is not
   planned misleads reviewers and creates a future-work debt the next
   paper cannot pay.
2. The in-situ cross-reference plan (ref17 =
   [S0132](https://doi.org/10.1088/0029-5515/55/11/113012)) is the correct
   future-work anchor and aligns with WP-C/campaign plans ΓÇö keep.

### 1.8 References (lines 551ΓÇô613)

- 20 entries; DOIs present except ref14 (Almagri 1998, no DOI recorded) and
  ref15 (PhD dissertation). Spot-verified against the ledger: ref2=S0131,
  ref6=[S0066](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/aa7867),
  ref10=[S0004](https://doi.org/10.1109/JSEN.2019.2895546), ref11=S0006,
  ref12=[S0017](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2201339), ref16/ref17 = HSX
  magnetics papers (ref17=S0132). No fabricated citation found. [EE]
- **Gap driving R2-03:** only four GaN-Hall-specific entries
  (ref10/11/12/15). The group's own most on-point GaN result ΓÇö micro-tesla
  offset via current spinning, [S0005](https://doi.org/10.1109/LSENS.2019.2898157),
  published in *IEEE Sensors Letters itself* ΓÇö is not cited. Also absent:
  recent GaN Hall work ([S0009](https://doi.org/10.1109/ises54909.2022.00071),
  [S0010](https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3539435),
  [S0016](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6501/ac12fe),
  [S0012](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0305414)) and most of the fusion Hall
  deployment lineage (S0069/S0070/S0113ΓÇôS0115/S0117/[S0143](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4894209)/[S0153](https://doi.org/10.3390/s21030721)).

---

## 2. Summary lists

**Claims exactly supported now (keep as-is in any revision):** A1, A3, A4,
A6, A7, M1ΓÇôM4, M6ΓÇôM9, R-1, R-2, R-4 (qualitative form), Fig. 1ΓÇô4 content.

**Claims requiring qualification or rewording (no new data needed):**

1. A2 ΓÇö QHS wording ΓåÆ match S0128 exactly.
2. A5 / I6 / R-3 ΓÇö shot-count and repeatability wording ΓåÆ recount +
   quantify from supplied data (┬º4.1).
3. I3 ΓÇö "cannot be deployed" ΓåÆ temperature/radiation-headroom framing with
   the non-GaN fusion Hall lineage cited as prior art.
4. I7 ΓÇö novelty claim ΓåÆ re-centered "first GaN/WBG in-vessel; first Hall in
   a QHS stellarator" with named bounding prior art.
5. R-5 ΓÇö "track magnetic-field dynamics" ΓåÆ voltage-domain/temporal wording
   until calibration lands.
6. Conclusion radiation sentence ΓåÆ TCAD/literature outlook only.

**Claims requiring new data before they can be made:**

1. Any tesla-denominated output, Fig. 5 in field units, absolute-field
   bounds (AE-01/AE-04/AE-05/R1-01 ΓåÆ WP-C bench calibration; blocked by the
   open ~109├ù anomaly C017). [PX ΓåÆ stage 40]
2. Fabrication-iteration repeatability statistics (AE-03/R2-02 ΓåÆ WP-B ΓëÑ3
   dies; die availability = advisor gate). [PX ΓåÆ stage 40]
3. A derived/measured bandwidth figure replacing the 1 MHz assertion
   (AE-07/R1-04 ΓåÆ chain analysis + bench sweep). [PX ΓåÆ stage 40]
4. Direct 1:1 field comparison against a conventional probe (R1-02 ΓåÆ UW
   data request first [GATE], else next campaign). [PX ΓåÆ stage 40]

---

## 3. Novelty-comparison dimensions for the GaN-sensor table (WP-A)

The AE asked for a performance comparison table (AE-02); R2's novelty
objection (R2-01) is answered at the same stroke if the table shows where
this work sits. No published review contains a unified GaN-Hall comparison
row set ([S0065](https://doi.org/10.1088/2631-8695/ac0838) has no GaN row) ΓÇö
the table is itself a small novelty contribution. [EE]

**Recommended dimensions (columns):**

1. Material system / channel (2DEG vs bulk vs metal film)
2. Voltage- or current-scaled sensitivity (state which; normalize units)
3. Demonstrated field range
4. Bandwidth **with its evidentiary basis** (measured/derived/asserted)
5. Raw offset and offset after cancellation (┬╡T-equivalent where given)
6. Noise floor / minimum detectable field (T/ΓêÜHz at stated frequency)
7. Demonstrated temperature range
8. Radiation-tolerance evidence (literature citation only ΓÇö no new
   radiation experiments, per scope rule)
9. Active area / die size
10. Packaging / environment compatibility (UHV, bakeout, GDC survival)
11. Deployment context (bench / accelerator / fusion device; in-vessel vs
    ex-vessel)
12. Calibration status (uncalibrated / bench / traceable per
    [S0051](https://doi.org/10.5194/jsss-9-391-2020))

**Candidate rows:** GaN/WBG: this work; S0004; S0005; S0006; S0016; S0017;
S0009; S0010; S0012. Non-GaN high-performance III-V for contrast:
[S0011](https://doi.org/10.1109/JSEN.2024.3507799),
[S0014](https://doi.org/10.1109/JSEN.2014.2368074). Fusion-deployed non-GaN
Hall anchors: S0068 (JET InSb), S0113ΓÇôS0115 (ITER bismuth), S0153
(ceramic-Cr), S0066 (gold-film/metal), S0070/S0117 (CASTOR), S0069 (EAST),
S0143 (CTH array).

**[GATE] carried from Stage 10D:** several candidate rows are
`metadata_only`/`abstract_metadata` in the ledger; every specific number
entering the table must first be re-confirmed against the primary PDF.

---

## 4. Recoverable from supplied data vs. data that does not exist

### 4.1 Recoverable by analysis alone (no hardware, no campaign)

From `../../07_HSX_august2025_results/hsx_20250821/` (73 `scope_N.csv`
voltage traces, `test_note.docx` shot manifest, shots 18ΓÇô21 density/
stored-energy `.dat`, coil-current logs for shots 65/68 ΓÇö spot-verified
this stage):

1. **Exact shot accounting** ΓÇö recount plasma vs coil-only vs unbiased
   shots from `test_note.docx`; fix the "68 consecutive plasma discharge
   shots" wording (A5) with the true auditable numbers.
2. **Operational repeatability statistics** ΓÇö per-shot ignition-transient
   amplitude/timing/shape-correlation distribution across all comparable
   biased plasma shots; converts R-3 from assertion to statistic. (Does
   **not** substitute for AE-03's fabrication-iteration statistics.)
3. **Quantified temporal correlation** ΓÇö cross-correlation coefficient and
   lag between sensor output and diamagnetic-loop stored energy for shots
   21/18/19, including direct measurement of the stated ~30 ms DAQ offset.
4. **Bias-scaling check** ΓÇö `test_note.docx` records 0.2ΓÇô0.4 V bias
   settings; verifying response Γê¥ V_bias in-situ would materially harden
   the Hall-origin argument (M8) against EMI/charge-artifact alternatives.
5. **In-situ voltage-noise floor** ΓÇö V/ΓêÜHz spectra in the HSX EMI
   environment from existing FFT pipelines (`.m` scripts present).
6. **Figure regeneration** ΓÇö Fig. 4/5 reproduction and the R1-05 overlay
   re-plot (in volts today; in field units only after WP-C).

### 4.2 Does not exist in supplied data and cannot be recovered from it

| Missing item | Why unrecoverable | Path |
|---|---|---|
| Any tesla value; S_v; calibration factor | No sensitivity/gain-to-field chain anywhere in the archive (Group C inventory) | WP-C bench calibration [PX] |
| V_off of the real GaN die | Never measured; emulator result (C016) does not transfer | WP-C [PX] |
| Verified chain gain / transfer function / bandwidth | Asserted only (C003/C004) | bench sweep [PX] |
| In-vessel sensor temperature during shots | No temperature log in archive | future campaign instrumentation [PX] |
| Multi-die statistics | One module ever deployed (C007) | WP-B [PX] |
| Co-located B-dot/pickup field data for 2025 shots | Not in archive; UW may hold it | [GATE] UW data request |
| Parasitic characterization (bonds, LCC, cabling) | Never measured | bench [PX] |

---

## 5. Statistical/repeatability and calibration gaps (consolidated)

1. **Calibration** ΓÇö the single blocking gap. No calibration attempt exists
   (C005); project 02's Helmholtz procedure is specified, not run (C013,
   conflict C6); the ~109├ù magnitude anomaly (C017) is an explicit
   do-not-calibrate-yet blocker that must close first. Norms to meet:
   traceable Hall calibration [S0051], GUM/Monte-Carlo uncertainty
   budget [S0220](https://doi.org/10.3390/s25051633), drift/Allan
   characterization [S0168](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIM.2007.908635).
2. **Fabrication repeatability** ΓÇö n=1 module deployed; zero die-to-die
   data. Bench-satisfiable per the AE's own concession (AE-03). Templates:
   on-chip Hall-cell statistics [S0218](https://doi.org/10.3390/jsan2010085);
   JET's 18-sensor stability record [S0068] as the field's bar.
3. **Operational repeatability** ΓÇö claimed qualitatively (R-3), quantifiable
   now from supplied data (┬º4.1.2) ΓÇö the cheapest credibility win available.
4. **Offset** ΓÇö the emulator spinning-current result (ΓëÑ130├ù suppression,
   C016) is real bench evidence but is **not** sensor evidence; in the
   revision it may be described only as readout-architecture validation,
   clearly labeled emulator-based, if mentioned at all.

## 6. Bandwidth and parasitic evidence gap (consolidated)

The 1 MHz claim appears twice (lines 453, 483) with no derivation in the
manuscript, its references, or `SPECS.md` (C003). R1-04 asks how it was
established; AE-07 generalizes to bandwidth/parasitics as the quantities
that determine tracking fidelity and class comparison; AE-08 offers
packaging-parasitics novelty if quantified. What exists today: component
identities (INA849, OPA814) and an underived "1 MHz raw BW" note. What is
needed: a measured chain transfer function with the limiting element
identified (device vs amplifier configuration vs cabling/feedthrough vs
acquisition), a bandwidth column in the WP-A table, and ΓÇö opportunistically
ΓÇö a packaging-parasitic characterization supporting AE-08's system framing.
Until then, the revision must not restate 1 MHz. [PX ΓåÆ stage 40]

## 7. Concise revision map (diagnosis only ΓÇö no edits performed)

| Manuscript location | Action in revision | Answers | Evidence prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title (370) | Keep only with field-unit results delivered | AE-01 | WP-C |
| Abstract (428) | Recount shots; S0128 QHS wording; add calibrated headline number (S_v ┬▒ u, field-unit result); drop/qualify "68 consecutive plasma" | AE-01, A2, A5 | WP-C + ┬º4.1.1 |
| Intro ┬╢1 (449) | Re-cite ref2 at Mirnov mention | R1-03 | none |
| Intro ┬╢2 (451) | Rewrite I3 as headroom argument; cite fusion Hall lineage as prior art | R2-01, I3 | none |
| Intro ┬╢3 (453) | Precise two-part first-claim; remove unsupported 1 MHz | I7, R1-04 | bench sweep for any stated BW |
| Methods II.C (483ΓÇô487) | State measured gain/BW with basis; add calibration summary sentence(s) per R1's page-limit concession | AE-04, AE-07, R1-01 | WP-C + sweep |
| Results III.A (496) | Replace qualitative repeatability with ┬º4.1.2 statistics; add bias-scaling check | R-3, M8 | analysis only |
| Results III.B (504) | Field-unit Fig. 5 with uncertainty bands; overlay format; quantified correlation + lag | AE-05, R1-05, R-4 | WP-C for units; analysis otherwise |
| NEW: comparison table | Insert WP-A table (┬º3) | AE-02, R2-01, R2-03 | analysis + primary-PDF re-confirmation |
| NEW: repeatability | WP-B multi-die bench statistics + single-module explanation | AE-03, R2-02 | WP-B + team input |
| Conclusion (506) | Remove neutron-facility promise ΓåÆ TCAD/literature outlook; keep S0132 cross-reference plan | ┬º1.7 | none |
| References | Add S0005 + GaN set + fusion-deployment set within the 4-page/reference-column budget | R2-03 | none |

**Fit check [INF]:** SENSL's 4-page limit (confirmed policy, see
[`03_PUBLICATION_ROUTE_DECISION.md`](03_PUBLICATION_ROUTE_DECISION.md) ┬º4)
is feasible because R1 explicitly allows calibration as text discussion,
the table replaces prose, and Fig. 5's overlay consolidates panels; the
likeliest cut is shortening III.B's discharge narratives (also AE-06's
request).

## 8. Flags for later stages

1. **Never describe the manuscript as published (2023 or otherwise)** in
   any revision, preprint, cover letter, or response letter ΓÇö conflict C1
   controls; it is a declined 2026 submission with an invitation to
   resubmit under a new ID.
2. Stage 40 owns the experiment specifications for WP-B/WP-C, the anomaly
   closure, the bench sweep, and the UW co-located-data request (R1-02).
3. Stage 50 owns the pre-disclosure IP screen the advisor required before
   any arXiv posting (user request, `../inputs/ORIGINAL_REQUEST.txt`).
4. The radiation future-work sentence (┬º1.7.1) must also be reconciled in
   project-03 planning documents when those are next revised (outside this
   mission's write scope).
5. 75/231 ledger rows are metadata-only: any number quoted into the WP-A
   table needs primary-source re-confirmation first (Stage 10D gate).

42	## 1. Design philosophy: minimum rigorous, fabrication-minimal, two-tier
43	
44	**Objective [REC]:** convert the existing voltage-domain HSX demonstration
45	into a defensible magnetic-field instrument study ΓÇö tesla-denominated
46	output with a written uncertainty budget, repeatability evidence, a
47	justified bandwidth figure, and (as upside) an in-machine absolute anchor
48	ΓÇö while adding **zero new device topology and zero cleanroom work**
49	(stage 20 ┬º7; MISSION.md low-cleanroom constraint).
50	
51	Three design rules govern everything below:
52	
53	1. **Bench before machine.** Every P0 reviewer item (AE-01, AE-03, AE-04,
54	   AE-05, R1-01, R2-02) is bench-satisfiable; the AE explicitly conceded
55	   in-vessel repetition is impractical and asked for bench repetition
56	   (matrix AE-03). The HSX campaign is upside and RSI material, not a
57	   single point of failure ΓÇö stage 20's structural improvement (fallback
58	   F1 at gate G2).
59	2. **Nothing is assumed available.** Equipment, dies, feedthroughs, shot
60	   time, and machine signals enter the plan only through the ┬º2 inventory
61	   gates. The supplied files establish surprisingly little as physically
62	   in-hand (see ┬º2) ΓÇö most of the 02 plan's testbench is *designed*, not
63	   *built* [SF: shopping list at 02 plan ┬º7.4; C013].
64	3. **Anomaly first.** The ~109├ù discrepancy (C017) carries an explicit
65	   do-not-calibrate instruction in the project's own journal [SF]. Every
66	   calibration requirement is gated behind B-01. A calibration built on an
67	   unexplained 109├ù gain error would be worse than no calibration.
68	
69	**Two-tier output** (matches the stage-30 route decision AΓåÆC):
70	- **Tier 1 ΓÇö SENSL resubmission package** (bench + supplied-data
71	  analyses only): ┬º11.1.
72	- **Tier 2 ΓÇö RSI instrument package** (adds campaign anchors, vector
73	  probe, stability): ┬º11.2.

143	## 3. Bench phase 0 ΓÇö chain verification (before any calibration)
144	
145	**B-01 ΓÇö anomaly closure (╬öV gain check)** [PX; inherited as project 02's
146	own named top priority, not invented here]. Static phases; inject ~1 mV
147	known differential (1.000 V through 10 k╬⌐:10 ╬⌐ divider) at the sense pair;
148	toggle; `╬öV_out/╬öV_in = G`. Target 100.3 ┬▒ 1 % (02 plan ┬º4 Day 3ΓÇô4).
149	Repeat at all 8 states (preferred design). In parallel, re-derive the
150	expected emulator output from DMM-measured ring resistances via
151	`o = I┬╖(R14┬╖R23 ΓêÆ R12┬╖R34)/╬úR` ΓÇö the 2026-07-08 run's 0.686 V vs ~75 V
152	prediction must resolve into either (a) in-operation gain Γëá 100.3 or
153	(b) the 2.2 k╬⌐ not electrically unbalancing the bridge as modeled
154	[SF: NOTES.md names exactly these two survivors]. **Exit criterion:** the
155	mechanism is named, reproduced, and written to the project 02 journal;
156	the do-not-calibrate flag is lifted. No calibration work starts before
157	this [REC ΓÇö hard rule].
158	
159	**B-02 ΓÇö static 8-state survey.** Emulator survey across all 8 mux states
160	must reproduce SPECS' sign pattern `+ ΓêÆ ΓêÆ + ΓêÆ + + ΓêÆ` with amplitude G┬╖o
161	predicted from measured resistors. Preferred: cross-check states 2/3/6/7
162	on the mode-2 Pico-ADC path ΓÇö this is also mode-2's first hardware
163	validation (it has only ever run stubbed [SF]), which D-01 and F-07 need.
164	
165	**Fix the global sign here and freeze it** (┬º5).

169	## 4. Bench calibration ΓÇö DC and frequency-dependent
170	
171	### 4.0 Campaign zero: the supplied-data analyses (run any time, no hardware)
172	
173	A-01ΓÇªA-06 ([`04_MEASUREMENT_REQUIREMENTS.csv`](04_MEASUREMENT_REQUIREMENTS.csv);
174	methods in [`04_DATA_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`](04_DATA_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md) ┬º3ΓÇô┬º5):
175	shot recount, operational-repeatability statistics, quantified
176	diamagnetic-loop correlation + measured DAQ offset, bias-scaling check,
177	in-situ voltage-noise floor, figure regeneration. These six close the
178	wording-level reviewer items (A5/R-3/R-4/M8) from the immutable 2025
179	archive alone [SF basis: stage 30 diagnosis ┬º4.1] and are the cheapest
180	credibility wins in the whole plan. Start them immediately ΓÇö they are
181	also the G1-fail hedge.
182	
183	### 4.1 Field source and traceability (C-01)
184	
185	Build the Helmholtz pair exactly per SPECS (R = 50 mm, N = 100/coil,
186	k Γëê 1.8 mT/A, ┬▒2.7 mT at ┬▒1.5 A) [SF: design exists; build does not].
187	Triangulate k three ways (02 plan ┬º7.2): geometry + 0.1 % shunt
188	(primary; the pair is a *calculable standard*, uniform to <0.1 % over the
189	die), AC pickup coil, and commercial reference sensors (E-01). Norm for
190	traceable Hall-probe calibration with a written budget:
191	[S0051](https://doi.org/10.5194/jsss-9-391-2020) [EE]. **Acceptance:**
192	u(k)/k Γëñ 2 %, methods consistent within stated uncertainties;
193	disagreements investigated, never averaged away [REC].
194	
195	### 4.2 DC calibration, current-bias mode (C-02 ΓÇö the WP-C core)
196	
197	Bipolar ΓëÑ11-point sweep over ┬▒2.7 mT at 100 ┬╡A; fit
198	`V_demod = m┬╖B + b`; up and down sweeps (hysteresis, C-06 free of
199	charge); ΓëÑ3 full repetitions on separate days with remount (feeds D-02).
200	Expected m Γëê 0.5ΓÇô0.6 V/T [SF: SPECS expectation ΓÇö to be tested, not
201	assumed]. Targets (02 plan ┬º7.3): **~2 % absolute, <0.5 % linearity**.
202	Cross-check m against first principles `G┬╖S_I┬╖I┬╖(loading Γëê 0.83)`; a
203	large gap re-opens B-01. Training/held-out field-point protocol per the
204	02 plan ┬º7.3 (leakage safeguard ΓÇö see
205	[`04_DATA_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`](04_DATA_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md) ┬º8).
206	
207	### 4.3 Voltage-bias-mode sensitivity for the retroactive conversion (C-03)
208	
209	**This row exists because the 2025 data was not taken with the 2026
210	readout.** The deployed chain was voltage-bias 0.2ΓÇô0.4 V through
211	INA849 + 2├ùOPA814 at G = 200 [SF: manuscript M3/M4; C004]. Converting the
212	2025 traces to tesla (AE-01/AE-05 ΓåÆ G-01) therefore needs **S_v at the
213	deployed bias settings for the deployed die** ΓÇö not the 100 ┬╡A
214	current-bias m. Measure S_v (V/V/T) at 0.2/0.3/0.4 V on the deployed die
215	(gate I-4), through the actual 2023 chain if it still exists (gate I-6),
216	else through a documented bench amplifier with the chain-gain-200
217	assumption stated. Every downstream tesla figure for 2025 data carries
218	the same-die/same-chain/temperature-transfer assumptions explicitly
219	(matrix AE-01 note). Fallback if the deployed die is gone: same-wafer
220	sibling + D-01's die-to-die spread as the transfer uncertainty, clearly
221	labeled [REC].
222	
223	### 4.4 Bias-current scaling (C-04)
224	
225	m at I = 50/100/200/500 ┬╡A; confirm m Γê¥ I; pick the HSX operating point
226	deliberately (noise-vs-I as the preferred add-on). If only a fixed
227	source exists, the linearity-in-I assumption is cited to prior GaN
228	characterization ([S0006](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.5139911),
229	[S0017](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.2201339)) and flagged as assumed [EE].
230	
231	### 4.5 Frequency-dependent calibration (B-03/B-04 ΓÇö closes AE-07/R1-04)
232	
233	- **Spun chain:** transfer function 10 HzΓÇô3 kHz (electrical injection
234	  minimum; Helmholtz sine drive preferred once C-01 exists) at
235	  f_spin = 10/40/100 kHz. Expected ΓêÆ3 dB near 1ΓÇô2 kHz from demod
236	  averaging [SF: SPECS]; measure, don't assert. Record **phase lag** ΓÇö
237	  required for honest correlation claims against the diamagnetic loop.
238	- **Static-phase (fast) chain:** electrical sweep to ΓêÆ3 dB; this is the
239	  fast-transient mode's real bandwidth.
240	- **The 1 MHz question (C003):** the revision states, for each chain
241	  generation, a bandwidth **with its evidentiary basis** (measured /
242	  derived / asserted ΓÇö asserted is retired). If the 2023 chain no longer
243	  exists (I-6), a derivation from the component configuration and
244	  acquisition settings is presented as derived-not-measured [REC].
245	  B-dot calibration methodology as the class norm:
246	  [S0076](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3246785) [EE].
247

250	## 5. Field-to-voltage transfer function, sign, and orientation
251	
252	Model chain (single axis) [SF: SPECS/plan; equations restated in
253	[`04_DATA_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`](04_DATA_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md) ┬º4]:
254	
255	- Current-bias 2026: `V_demod = m┬╖B_ΓèÑ + b`, `m = G┬╖L┬╖S_I┬╖I`
256	  (G gain, L loading Γëê 0.83, S_I Γëê 60 V/A/T, I bias) ΓÇö every factor
257	  measured, none trusted from SPECS without the ┬º3ΓÇô┬º4 checks.
258	- Voltage-bias 2023/2025: `V_out = A_v┬╖S_v┬╖V_bias┬╖B_ΓèÑ + A_v┬╖V_off(T)`
259	  (C023) ΓÇö S_v from C-03; V_off is why only calibrated-slope and
260	  AC/transient components convert cleanly (analysis plan ┬º4.2).
261	
262	**Sign/orientation protocol [REC, from the 02 plan ┬º1 caveat]:**
263	1. The demod sign rule (`+1 if a0 == a2`) comes from the netlist; the
264	   **global** sign does not ΓÇö fix it once with a NdFeB magnet of known
265	   polarity (I-3 purchase) and freeze it in firmware/analysis.
266	2. Record which plate normal maps to +B, photograph the die-in-LCC
267	   orientation, and carry that into the mount drawing.
268	3. At HSX, the surveyed pose (F-02) + the UW field model's field
269	   direction at the pose (U-4) close the orientation loop: predicted
270	   sign of the coil-only response is a pass/fail check on installation
271	   day (F-01 acceptance includes sign).
272	4. B_ΓèÑ is the normal component only: the cos-error term (<3┬░ ΓåÆ 0.15 %
273	   [SF: 02 plan ┬º7.3]) enters the budget; in-plane (planar-Hall) response
274	   is checked at bench by driving B in-plane (03 plan ┬º3.2 method,
275	   single-axis version) [PX].

296	## 7. Device/module repeatability (WP-B) ΓÇö with the honest single-device fallback
297	
298	### 7.1 Multi-die design (D-01, the AE's own specification)
299	
300	ΓëÑ3 packaged dies (the AE's number [SF: decision letter]), same fabrication
301	lineage, existing iterations only ΓÇö 2023-generation remainders and/or
302	gen-2 if fabricated (advisor decision 3; gates I-4/I-5). Per die: mode-2
303	raw-offset at 100 ┬╡A (the incoming-inspection tool the 03 plan ┬º2.1
304	already designates [SF]) and a ΓëÑ5-point Helmholtz sensitivity spot-sweep.
305	ΓëÑ3 repeats per die so within-die variance is separable from between-die
306	variance (variance decomposition in
307	[`04_UNCERTAINTY_AND_STATISTICS_PLAN.md`](04_UNCERTAINTY_AND_STATISTICS_PLAN.md)
308	┬º4). Literature templates: on-chip Hall-cell statistics
309	[S0218](https://doi.org/10.3390/jsan2010085); the group's own geometry/
310	offset statistics [S0004](https://doi.org/10.1109/JSEN.2019.2895546);
311	JET's 18-sensor multi-year stability as the field's bar
312	[S0068](https://doi.org/10.1088/1741-4326/ac8aad) [EE].
313	
314	### 7.2 Setup-vs-device separation (D-02)
315	
316	ΓëÑ3 full remove-remount-recalibrate cycles on one die (plus a thermal
317	cycle preferred). Without this, D-01's between-die spread is confounded
318	with fixture repeatability [INF].
319	
320	### 7.3 Honest single-device fallback [REC]
321	
322	If gates I-4/I-5 yield only one packaged die and no packaging path:
323	1. Report D-02 remount repeatability as **operational** repeatability ΓÇö
324	   never as fabrication repeatability.
325	2. Cite prior-literature die statistics that genuinely cover the claim
326	   (S0004, S0218) ΓÇö the AE explicitly allows this route if "shown

377	(photogrammetry cross-check preferred; re-survey after the run). The pose

379	field model supplies the local gradient (add to U-4). If no survey is

## 1. Design philosophy: minimum rigorous, fabrication-minimal, two-tier

**Objective [REC]:** convert the existing voltage-domain HSX demonstration
into a defensible magnetic-field instrument study ΓÇö tesla-denominated
output with a written uncertainty budget, repeatability evidence, a
justified bandwidth figure, and (as upside) an in-machine absolute anchor
ΓÇö while adding **zero new device topology and zero cleanroom work**
(stage 20 ┬º7; MISSION.md low-cleanroom constraint).

Three design rules govern everything below:

1. **Bench before machine.** Every P0 reviewer item (AE-01, AE-03, AE-04,
   AE-05, R1-01, R2-02) is bench-satisfiable; the AE explicitly conceded
   in-vessel repetition is impractical and asked for bench repetition
   (matrix AE-03). The HSX campaign is upside and RSI material, not a
   single point of failure ΓÇö stage 20's structural improvement (fallback
   F1 at gate G2).
2. **Nothing is assumed available.** Equipment, dies, feedthroughs, shot
   time, and machine signals enter the plan only through the ┬º2 inventory
   gates. The supplied files establish surprisingly little as physically
   in-hand (see ┬º2) ΓÇö most of the 02 plan's testbench is *designed*, not
   *built* [SF: shopping list at 02 plan ┬º7.4; C013].
3. **Anomaly first.** The ~109├ù discrepancy (C017) carries an explicit
   do-not-calibrate instruction in the project's own journal [SF]. Every
   calibration requirement is gated behind B-01. A calibration built on an
   unexplained 109├ù gain error would be worse than no calibration.

- **Tier 1 ΓÇö SENSL resubmission package** (bench + supplied-data

## 4. Bench calibration ΓÇö DC and frequency-dependent

### 4.0 Campaign zero: the supplied-data analyses (run any time, no hardware)

### 4.1 Field source and traceability (C-01)

k Γëê 1.8 mT/A, ┬▒2.7 mT at ┬▒1.5 A) [SF: design exists; build does not].
Triangulate k three ways (02 plan ┬º7.2): geometry + 0.1 % shunt
(primary; the pair is a *calculable standard*, uniform to <0.1 % over the
die), AC pickup coil, and commercial reference sensors (E-01). Norm for
traceable Hall-probe calibration with a written budget:
[S0051](https://doi.org/10.5194/jsss-9-391-2020) [EE]. **Acceptance:**
u(k)/k Γëñ 2 %, methods consistent within stated uncertainties;
disagreements investigated, never averaged away [REC].

### 4.2 DC calibration, current-bias mode (C-02 ΓÇö the WP-C core)

Bipolar ΓëÑ11-point sweep over ┬▒2.7 mT at 100 ┬╡A; fit
`V_demod = m┬╖B + b`; up and down sweeps (hysteresis, C-06 free of
charge); ΓëÑ3 full repetitions on separate days with remount (feeds D-02).
Expected m Γëê 0.5ΓÇô0.6 V/T [SF: SPECS expectation ΓÇö to be tested, not
assumed]. Targets (02 plan ┬º7.3): **~2 % absolute, <0.5 % linearity**.
Cross-check m against first principles `G┬╖S_I┬╖I┬╖(loading Γëê 0.83)`; a
large gap re-opens B-01. Training/held-out field-point protocol per the
02 plan ┬º7.3 (leakage safeguard ΓÇö see
[`04_DATA_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md`](04_DATA_ANALYSIS_PLAN.md) ┬º8).

### 4.3 Voltage-bias-mode sensitivity for the retroactive conversion (C-03)

**This row exists because the 2025 data was not taken with the 2026
readout.** The deployed chain was voltage-bias 0.2ΓÇô0.4 V through
INA849 + 2├ùOPA814 at G = 200 [SF: manuscript M3/M4; C004]. Converting the
2025 traces to tesla (AE-01/AE-05 ΓåÆ G-01) therefore needs **S_v at the
deployed bias settings for the deployed die** ΓÇö not the 100 ┬╡A

(gate I-4), through the actual 2023 chain if it still exists (gate I-6),

sibling + D-01's die-to-die spread as the transfer uncertainty, clearly
labeled [REC].

deliberately (noise-vs-I as the preferred add-on). If only a fixed

405	once ΓÇö they are the *same* critical path (┬º2.1) with the upside plan
406	adding parallel workstreams on top. Nothing in ┬º7.2 competes for the
407	critical-path resources that ┬º7.1 needs; the only real trade-off is Tim's
408	personal time and attention, which M28's explicit checkpoint exists to
409	manage deliberately rather than by drift.
410	
411	---
412	
413	## 8. Decision points if HSX access, hardware, calibration, repeatability, or publication review slips
414	
415	| Slip scenario | Detection point | Decision | Fallback already defined | Effect on graduation date |
416	|---|---|---|---|---|
417	| **HSX access** (campaign #1 or #2 cannot happen at all) | U-9 unconfirmed by ~Sep 2026 (campaign 1) or M25 fails entirely (campaign 2) | Advisor + Tim (M28-style checkpoint) | Fallback F1 (campaign 1): P1 unaffected, bench-only by design. Fallback F2 (campaign 2): P3 descopes to bench-validated module (04_HSX_EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md ┬º8) | **None** if only campaign 2 is lost (MVG plan, ┬º7.1); **material risk** if HSX access is lost entirely ΓÇö this is stage-20's named reversal condition 3 (┬º11), which would push the whole direction toward the OPT3 fallback |
418	| **Hardware** (die supply insufficient, bond yield fails, board fault) | M02 (die-supply decision) or M05/M21 (inventory/build gates) | Tim + advisor | Single-device WP-B fallback (┬º7.3 of the experiment plan); 2-axis vector-probe fallback (gate G3) | None for MVG; upside plan's vector-probe chapter becomes 2-axis instead of 3-axis |
419	| **Calibration** (the ~109├ù anomaly does not resolve) | M06 (gate G1) | Tim + advisor ΓÇö board fault-isolation sprint | P1 re-scoped around A-group + WP-A + bandwidth only, calibration claim dropped (04_HSX_EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md G1-fail branch) | **Material risk to the critical path** ΓÇö this is the single highest-leverage failure mode in the whole plan, because P1, P2's WP-D validation, and the entire tesla-denominated claim set all sit downstream of it |
420	| **Repeatability** (only 1 die, no packaging path) | M02/M05 (I-5) | Tim + advisor | Honest single-device fallback: report remount repeatability as operational, cite literature (S0004/S0218) for population statistics ΓÇö the AE explicitly allows this route | None ΓÇö this is a pre-planned, AE-sanctioned degradation, not an improvised one |
421	| **Publication review** (P1 or P2 declined a second time) | M20/M26 (P1); M27/M31 (P2) | Advisor escalation | P1: another Sensors-class venue, or a strengthened Route-D-style arXiv posting (03_PUBLICATION_ROUTE_DECISION.md ┬º3.4/┬º6). P2: revise and resubmit; a P2 decline is flagged as a graduation-risk trigger because it is the MVG plan's second required paper | **Direct risk to the MVG floor** if P2 fails and no revision succeeds in time ΓÇö the one scenario in this table with no fully pre-planned fallback, because it removes the plan's second paper rather than degrading a chapter |
422	
423	---
424	
425	## 9. Weekly operating rhythm and measurable progress indicators
426	
427	### 9.1 Weekly operating rhythm [REC]
428	
429	- **One fixed weekly checkpoint** (day/time chosen by Tim) reviewing: what
430	  closed this week against the active milestone(s) in
431	  `06_MILESTONES.csv`, what is blocked and on whom, and whether any
432	  `slip_trigger` condition has been hit.
433	- **Bench/desk time protected in blocks**, not interleaved hour-by-hour ΓÇö
434	  the stage-40 burden estimates (┬º12.1) assume single-operator, serial
435	  bench work; context-switching between bench calibration and manuscript
436	  writing in the same day is a documented efficiency loss in that plan.
437	- **Advisor sync cadence:** at minimum, once per the gates in
438	  `06_ADVISOR_MEETING_BRIEF.md` (M02, M13, M28, M34) ΓÇö not necessarily
439	  weekly, but never less often than monthly during the AugΓÇôDec 2026
440	  bench-and-campaign-dense period.
441	- **Startup workstream check-in:** monthly, ~1 day, deliberately
442	  lightweight (M41/M43) so it never competes with critical-path time.
443	
444	### 9.2 Measurable progress indicators [REC]
445	
446	| Indicator | How measured | Where tracked |
447	|---|---|---|
448	| Milestones closed vs. planned | Count of `status=complete` rows in `06_MILESTONES.csv` vs. rows whose `target_date` has passed | Weekly checkpoint |
449	| Bench-days consumed vs. the ~19ΓÇô29 day Tier-1 estimate | Logged bench-days per session | Project 02 journal (existing practice) |
450	| Open gates | Count of unresolved I-/U-/G- gates from stage 40, and G-A..G-H from stage 50 | This roadmap's ┬º1 + `05_DISCLOSURE_HOLD_CHECKLIST.md` |
451	| Papers in each state (drafting / submitted / in review / accepted) | P1/P2/P3 status | `06_MILESTONES.csv` P1-MANUSCRIPT / WPD-ARCH / P3-MANUSCRIPT rows |
452	| Dissertation chapters drafted vs. 7 planned | Chapter count | M36/M37 |
453	| Committee/registration milestones met on schedule | M32/M33/M38/M39 dates vs. actual | Weekly checkpoint |
454	| Direction-gate conditions (G5, M34) | Binary: accepted/in-revision paper? real-die calibration achieved? | Advisor sync |
455	
456	---
457	
458	## 10. Cross-references
459	
460	- Milestone-level detail, dates, dependencies, owners, and fallbacks for
461	  every item named above: [`06_MILESTONES.csv`](06_MILESTONES.csv).
462	- Advisor-facing summary of the decisions this roadmap assumes get made
463	  early (M01ΓÇôM03, M13, M28, M34): [`06_ADVISOR_MEETING_BRIEF.md`](06_ADVISOR_MEETING_BRIEF.md).
464	- Startup-preparation detail for the STARTUP workstream (M41ΓÇôM44):

466	- This document deliberately does not re-derive the direction, venue

Prepared by: Claude Code, stage `60_timeline`, requested model Sonnet 5 /

University Oral Examination in year 4:

convention: **[SF]** supplied fact, **[EE]** external evidence, **[INF]**
inference, **[REC]** recommendation, **[PX]** proposed experiment,

**Standing corrections honored (conflicts C1/C6):** the manuscript is a

---

## 1. Ground truth this roadmap starts from

- **Today:** 2026-07-25 [SF]. Tim begins his third PhD year in Fall 2026
  and wants to graduate in about two years ΓÇö i.e., by roughly **summer
  2028** [SF, `../inputs/ORIGINAL_REQUEST.txt`].

- **The direction verdict (stage 20):** continue the GaN Hall

  urgency, with CC-2 (readout chain) and CC-1 (packaging stack) most
  urgent because the P1 manuscript discloses them first [SF,
  `05_CANDIDATE_PROTECTABLE_CONCEPTS.md` ┬º0].
- **A schedule reconciliation this stage performs [REC]:** stage 20's P3
  window (months 12ΓÇô24 Γëê Aug 2027ΓÇôAug 2028) and project 03's own "~March
  2027" RSI-submission target both derive from the same Nov-2026
  campaign-#2 date with a ~Feb-2027 slip limit for "P3-as-planned." This

  the ambiguity stage 30 handed forward for stage 60 to resolve
  (`03_PUBLICATION_ROUTE_DECISION.md` ┬º7).
- **A schedule-honesty flag [REC]:** the stage-40 target for HSX campaign
  #1 is **August 2026** [SF, U-9/C018] ΓÇö about three weeks from today. The
  pre-ship dependency chain (anomaly closure ΓåÆ calibration ΓåÆ
  module-health check) makes that target very tight; ┬º3 below shows both
  the stated target and a realistic case sliding into September 2026. The
  existing fallback (F1: "P1 is bench-only and unaffected") absorbs this

---

## 2. Critical path and parallel workstreams

### 2.1 The single critical path to graduation

The shortest chain of dependencies that **must** all succeed for an
on-schedule defense is:

```
G0 inventory (M05) -> B-01 anomaly closure / G1 (M06) -> WP-C calibration
(M08-M10) -> P1 draft (M14) -> IP screen (M13) -> P1 resubmission (M18)
-> P1 review (M20) -> P1 acceptance (M26) -> P2 draft/submit (M27) ->
P2 acceptance (M31) -> dissertation Ch.1-4 (M36) + Ch.5,7 (from M37) ->
reading committee (M32) + candidacy (M33) -> TGR (M38) -> oral exam/
defense (M39) -> dissertation submitted (M40)
```

This path **never requires the HSX campaign to succeed** [REC ΓÇö this is
the structural improvement OPT2 buys over OPT1, stage 20 ┬º3.2].
*[Stage-70 clarification: the `M26 -> M27` arrow above shows the
acceptance sequence of the two-paper floor, not a work dependency ΓÇö
in `06_MILESTONES.csv` M27 (P2 drafting) depends only on M17/M23 and
proceeds in parallel with P1's review, exactly as ┬º3's January-2027
entry describes.]* Campaign
#1 (M16), the vector probe (M21ΓÇôM22), campaign #2 (M25), and the RSI paper
(M29/M30/M35) are all **parallel upside workstreams** that feed a stronger
dissertation and a third paper, but a slip in any of them degrades the
*upside* plan (┬º7.2), not the minimum-viable one (┬º7.1).

### 2.2 Parallel workstreams and their relationship to the critical path

| Workstream (CSV tag) | Feeds the critical path? | Role |
|---|---|---|
| BENCH-CAL (WP-C) | **Yes** | On the critical path ΓÇö P1 cannot claim calibration without it |
| REPEAT (WP-B) | **Yes** | On the critical path ΓÇö AE explicitly required repeatability evidence |
| ANALYSIS (A-group, WP-A) | **Yes**, but lowest-risk | Needs nothing but the immutable 2025 archive; start immediately |
| P1-MANUSCRIPT | **Yes** | The critical-path spine |
| IP-DISCLOSURE | **Yes** (as a gate) | Blocks P1 resubmission and any arXiv posting ΓÇö cannot be skipped |
| CAMPAIGN-1 | No (upside) | Feeds WP-D data and the in-situ anchor; P1 does not depend on it |
| WPD-ARCH (P2) | **Yes** (for the MVG floor) | The second paper of the stage-20 two-paper floor; degrades gracefully without campaign data |
| VECTOR-HW / CAMPAIGN-2 / P3-MANUSCRIPT | No (upside) | The RSI capstone; genuinely optional for graduation, core to the "stronger upside" plan |
| DISSERTATION | **Yes** | Committee/registration process runs in parallel with research from month 1 |
| STARTUP | No | Explicitly designed to never gate a research milestone (06_STARTUP_READINESS.md) |

**Implication [REC]:** if time or resources become scarce, cut from
CAMPAIGN-2/VECTOR-HW/P3 first (┬º7.1's minimum-viable-graduation plan), not
from BENCH-CAL/REPEAT/ANALYSIS/P1/P2/DISSERTATION.

---

## 3. Month-by-month detail ΓÇö first six months (Aug 2026 ΓÇô Jan 2027)

### August 2026 ΓÇö inventory, anomaly closure, analysis kickoff

- Advisor decision batch #1 (M02) and the UW e-mail (M03, gate G-A) open

  (die supply, UW data access, campaign authorization).
- A-group supplied-data analyses (M04) and the WP-A comparison table
  (M07) start immediately ΓÇö they need nothing but files already in hand
  and are the cheapest credibility wins in the entire plan [SF,
  `04_HSX_EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md` ┬º4.0].
- G0 inventory gates close (M05); the ~109├ù anomaly closure (M06, gate
  G1) is the month's single highest-priority bench task ΓÇö **no
  calibration work starts before it** [REC ΓÇö hard rule inherited from
  stage 40 ┬º1].
- Advisor + OTL pre-disclosure conversation opens (M13) ΓÇö it must
  conclude before the P1 draft (M14) can be resubmitted, so starting it
  in parallel with bench work, not after, is what keeps it off the
  critical path's tail.
- Campaign-#1 pre-ship work begins (M15); the stated Aug-2026 target
  (U-9/C018) is tight against this chain ΓÇö realistic execution slides

### September 2026 ΓÇö calibration core, repeatability, campaign #1, vector build starts

- WP-C calibration core: field-source build (M08), DC calibration +
  uncertainty budget (M09), voltage-bias S_v for the retroactive 2025
  conversion (M10) ΓÇö this is the month's spine.

- Campaign #1 executes (M16, realistic window) ΓÇö coil-only anchor +

- Vector-probe cube build starts (M21, gate G3) ΓÇö this is on the
  campaign-#2 critical path (not the graduation critical path), so
  starting it now rather than after P1 ships keeps the RSI upside alive
  without slowing P1.
- Dissertation reading committee formation opens (M32) ΓÇö pure
  administrative parallel track; start it now because Stanford EE's own

### October 2026 ΓÇö P1 drafting, vector calibration, WP-D development

- P1 full draft (M14) ΓÇö the month's central task, integrating every
  bench result from AugustΓÇôSeptember.
- Vector-probe matrix calibration (M22) continues; WP-D algorithm
  development on synthetic + 2025 data (M17, started September) continues
  in parallel ΓÇö this is software-heavy, desk-based work that does not
  compete for bench time with M08ΓÇôM12.
- IP screen (M13) should conclude by month's end ΓÇö it is the hard gate
  on both P1 resubmission and any UW-facing disclosure of CC-3/CC-5

### November 2026 ΓÇö P1 resubmission, optional arXiv, campaign #2 window opens

- P1 resubmission to IEEE Sensors Letters (M18) ΓÇö contingent on the IP
  screen (M13) being closed; if it is not, this slips, not the reverse

- Optional arXiv posting of the revised manuscript (M19, gate G-C) ΓÇö only
  with documented advisor + OTL sign-off.
- Campaign #2 pre-ship (M24) and the HSX deployment itself (M25, gate G4)
  open their window ΓÇö stated target is Nov 2026, hard slip limit ~Feb
  2027 for "P3-as-planned" (┬º1's reconciliation).

### December 2026 ΓÇö review cycle, campaign-#2 continuation, committee filing

- SENSL review cycle (M20) is now underway ΓÇö timeline is journal-
  controlled, not something this plan can accelerate.
- Campaign #2 continues through its Nov-2026ΓÇôFeb-2027 window (M25).
- Dissertation reading committee (M32) target-completes this month.
- Startup discovery round 1 (M41) runs quietly in the background ΓÇö ~1
  day/month, never competing with the above for bench or writing time.

### January 2027 ΓÇö P1 acceptance track, P2 drafting begins, candidacy opens

- P1 acceptance decision expected in this window (M26) ΓÇö first
  first-author accepted paper, if the review cycle is consistent with the
  journal's stated "Submission-to-ePublication = 4.8 weeks, median"
  statistic [EE, `03_PUBLICATION_ROUTE_DECISION.md` ┬º4.1; stage-70
  correction: this figure is the journal's submission-to-ePublication
  median, not a post-acceptance interval ΓÇö the M18ΓåÆM26 window already
  budgets ~2ΓÇô4├ù that median for re-review].
- P2 (hybrid-architecture) draft begins (M27), building on M17/M23.
- Candidacy/course-requirement confirmation opens (M33) ΓÇö parallel
  administrative track.

---

## 4. Quarterly detail ΓÇö months 7ΓÇô24 (Feb 2027 ΓÇô Jul 2028)

### Q1 2027 (FebΓÇôApr 2027)

- MVG-vs-upside checkpoint (M28) ΓÇö an explicit, dated decision, not a
  drift: once campaign #2's actual status (on schedule, slipped, or
  failed) is known, Tim and the advisor jointly commit to either the
  minimum-viable-graduation plan (┬º7.1) or continue chasing the 3-paper
  upside (┬º7.2).
- P2 submission (M27 target) and, in the upside case, P3 draft/submission
  (M29) both land in this window ΓÇö this is the plan's busiest writing
  quarter; the buffer described in ┬º8 exists precisely because of this
  clustering.
- Direction gate G5 approaches (M34, targeted ~Jul 2027) ΓÇö begin
  assembling its two required conditions (an accepted/in-revision
  first-author paper, and real-die absolute calibration) now rather than
  scrambling in June.

### Q2ΓÇôQ3 2027 (AprΓÇôSep 2027)

- P2 review/acceptance (M31) ΓÇö completes the stage-20 minimum-viable
  two-paper floor if it lands.
- In the realistic/fallback case, P3's descoped draft (M30) is written
  here instead of the upside-case M29 draft.
- Direction gate G5 (M34) executes at month 12 (~Jul 2027) ΓÇö the
  stage-20-mandated checkpoint on whether to continue OPT2 or pivot
  toward OPT3 (stage 20 ┬º8/┬º11).
- Dissertation chapters 1ΓÇô4 drafting begins (M36) ΓÇö these chapters are
  largely P1-paper content repackaged, so they are the lowest-risk
  writing and should not wait for P2/P3 to finish.
- Startup discovery round 2 + technical-validation summary (M43) starts,

### Q4 2027 ΓÇô Q1 2028 (Oct 2027 ΓÇô Mar 2028)

### Q2 2028 (AprΓÇôJun 2028)

### Q3 2028 (JunΓÇôJul 2028)

- Dissertation submission and degree conferral (M40) ΓÇö administrative
  buffer already built into the M39ΓåÆM40 gap.
- **This is the ~2-year-from-now graduation target the user asked for**,
  and it is also, per the external evidence in ┬º1, close to Stanford EE's
  own typical year-4 defense timing ΓÇö i.e., the accelerated-sounding ask

  is not behind on committee milestones, not a compression relative to

## 5. HSX/bench campaign preparation, data analysis, manuscript sequence, dissertation chapters, committee gates, and buffer ΓÇö cross-reference table

| Category | Milestones (CSV IDs) | Buffer built in |
|---|---|---|
| Bench campaign prep | M05, M06, M08ΓÇôM12, M15, M24 | ~2ΓÇô3 bench-days of slack per block per stage-40 ┬º12.1 estimates |
| Data analysis | M04, M07, M17, M23 | None needed ΓÇö desk-only, lowest risk |
| Manuscript sequence | M14, M18ΓÇôM20, M26 (P1); M27, M31 (P2); M29/M30, M35 (P3) | Review-cycle duration is journal-controlled (M20); the Q1 2027 clustering (┬º4) is the plan's tightest point |
| Dissertation chapters | M36 (Ch.1ΓÇô4), M37 (Ch.5ΓÇô7) | ~1 month slack in each chapter block before the M38 TGR gate |
| Committee/advisor gates | M02, M28, M32, M33, M34, M38, M39 | Reading committee (M32) deliberately starts in month 1ΓÇô4, far ahead of the M38 TGR need |
| Explicit buffer | Q3 2028 (M39ΓåÆM40 gap, ┬º4) | ~2 months between defense and submission for formatting/administrative delay |

---

## 6. Low-cleanroom allocation and what to avoid

Per the stage-20 direction decision (┬º7) and stage-40 experiment plan
(┬º12.2), **zero cleanroom steps appear anywhere in this roadmap** [SF]:

- The die is the established AlGaN/GaN Hall cross from the group's
  published lineage; gen-2's larger bond pads are a packaging-layout
  change, not a device innovation.
- Everything device-adjacent in M11/M21 (packaging, wedge bonding, EPO-TEK
  encapsulation, vacuum bake, ceramic-cube machining) is **assembly-lab**
  work, reusing the proven 2023 process verbatim ΓÇö not cleanroom
  fabrication.
- **What to avoid [REC]:** any new epitaxy, new mask sets beyond the
  pad-size change, any device-topology escalation (the rejected OPT4
  path, stage 20 ┬º3.4), and ΓÇö per the mission's fixed scope rule ΓÇö any
  neutron/gamma radiation experiment. Radiation stays literature/TCAD
  outlook only, cited at most as a sentence, never as Tim's own
  experimental work (parent `CLAUDE.md` scope rule; M37's dissertation
  guidance restates this explicitly).
- The heaviest hardware task in the whole 24 months is hand-assembling
  vector-probe board copies (M21) ΓÇö and that is upside/RSI scope (┬º7.2),
  not required for the minimum-viable plan (┬º7.1).

---

## 7. Minimum viable graduation plan and stronger upside plan

### 7.1 Minimum viable graduation (MVG) plan

**Structure:** P1 (SENSL, accepted) + P2 (hybrid-architecture paper,
accepted) = the stage-20-defined **minimum-viable two-paper floor**
[SF, `02_RESEARCH_DIRECTION_DECISION.md` ┬º6]. Neither depends on the HSX
campaign succeeding. The dissertation's vector-probe chapter (Ch.6, M37)
is written around the **bench-validated vector module and design** rather
than a completed in-vessel instrument study, with the campaign-#2 gap
stated as an explicit limitation and future-work item ΓÇö never hidden.

**What triggers committing to this plan [REC]:** the MVG-vs-upside
checkpoint (M28) is the formal decision point; the concrete trigger is
campaign #2 (M25) slipping past its ~Feb-2027 hard limit (fallback F2,
stage 20 ┬º8), or the direction gate G5 (M34) failing one of its two
conditions.

**What it requires that is not yet guaranteed:**
- The anomaly (M06/G1) must close ΓÇö without it, no calibration claim
  exists and P1 cannot make the finished-study claim the AE demanded.
- The die-supply decision (M02, advisor decision #3) must yield at least
  the honest single-device fallback path (┬º7.3 of
  `04_HSX_EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md`) for WP-B.
- P2 must clear its own novelty risk ΓÇö fresh 2025 Kalman-fusion
  literature (PA-N19/N20) is the field's own answer to "has this been
  done," and stage 20 ┬º11 already names this as a reversal condition to
  watch.

**Defense readiness under MVG:** M39 explicitly allows defending on
P1+P2 with a bench-validated-module framing for the vector-probe
material ΓÇö this is a **defensible thesis**, not a degraded one; it is
exactly the two-paper floor stage 20 scored as achievable "entirely on
bench + already-collected data."

### 7.2 Stronger upside plan

**Structure:** P1 + P2 + P3, all accepted, with campaign #1 and campaign
#2 both succeeding close to their stated targets (M16, M25). The
dissertation gains a full instrument-study chapter (RSI genre: calibrated
vector probe, uncertainty budget, in-situ validation) rather than a
descoped one. IP screening (M13, M24) may surface something OTL considers
worth a provisional filing ΓÇö stage 50 found the prior-art density high
enough that any protectable scope is expected to be thin, so this is
described as possible, not likely [SF, `05_CANDIDATE_PROTECTABLE_CONCEPTS.md`
┬º0, ┬º7]. Startup readiness work (M41ΓÇôM44) has a materially stronger
evidence base to draw on: a completed calibrated instrument, a quantified
hybrid-architecture result, and (if campaign #2 lands) a full vector-probe
demonstration ΓÇö see `06_STARTUP_READINESS.md` ┬º5 for what "stronger
evidence base" means concretely.

**What it requires beyond the MVG plan:** everything in ┬º7.1, plus
campaign #2 landing within its window (M25), the vector-probe hardware
build succeeding at ΓëÑ2 axes (M21, gate G3 ΓÇö the 2-axis fallback is itself
still publishable), and P3 clearing RSI's "not previously peer-reviewed"
duplication rule against P1/P2 content (M35).

**Relationship between the two plans [REC]:** they are not a fork taken
once ΓÇö they are the *same* critical path (┬º2.1) with the upside plan
adding parallel workstreams on top. Nothing in ┬º7.2 competes for the
critical-path resources that ┬º7.1 needs; the only real trade-off is Tim's
personal time and attention, which M28's explicit checkpoint exists to
manage deliberately rather than by drift.

---

## 8. Decision points if HSX access, hardware, calibration, repeatability, or publication review slips

| Slip scenario | Detection point | Decision | Fallback already defined | Effect on graduation date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **HSX access** (campaign #1 or #2 cannot happen at all) | U-9 unconfirmed by ~Sep 2026 (campaign 1) or M25 fails entirely (campaign 2) | Advisor + Tim (M28-style checkpoint) | Fallback F1 (campaign 1): P1 unaffected, bench-only by design. Fallback F2 (campaign 2): P3 descopes to bench-validated module (04_HSX_EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md ┬º8) | **None** if only campaign 2 is lost (MVG plan, ┬º7.1); **material risk** if HSX access is lost entirely ΓÇö this is stage-20's named reversal condition 3 (┬º11), which would push the whole direction toward the OPT3 fallback |
| **Hardware** (die supply insufficient, bond yield fails, board fault) | M02 (die-supply decision) or M05/M21 (inventory/build gates) | Tim + advisor | Single-device WP-B fallback (┬º7.3 of the experiment plan); 2-axis vector-probe fallback (gate G3) | None for MVG; upside plan's vector-probe chapter becomes 2-axis instead of 3-axis |
| **Calibration** (the ~109├ù anomaly does not resolve) | M06 (gate G1) | Tim + advisor ΓÇö board fault-isolation sprint | P1 re-scoped around A-group + WP-A + bandwidth only, calibration claim dropped (04_HSX_EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md G1-fail branch) | **Material risk to the critical path** ΓÇö this is the single highest-leverage failure mode in the whole plan, because P1, P2's WP-D validation, and the entire tesla-denominated claim set all sit downstream of it |
| **Repeatability** (only 1 die, no packaging path) | M02/M05 (I-5) | Tim + advisor | Honest single-device fallback: report remount repeatability as operational, cite literature (S0004/S0218) for population statistics ΓÇö the AE explicitly allows this route | None ΓÇö this is a pre-planned, AE-sanctioned degradation, not an improvised one |
| **Publication review** (P1 or P2 declined a second time) | M20/M26 (P1); M27/M31 (P2) | Advisor escalation | P1: another Sensors-class venue, or a strengthened Route-D-style arXiv posting (03_PUBLICATION_ROUTE_DECISION.md ┬º3.4/┬º6). P2: revise and resubmit; a P2 decline is flagged as a graduation-risk trigger because it is the MVG plan's second required paper | **Direct risk to the MVG floor** if P2 fails and no revision succeeds in time ΓÇö the one scenario in this table with no fully pre-planned fallback, because it removes the plan's second paper rather than degrading a chapter |

---

## 9. Weekly operating rhythm and measurable progress indicators

### 9.1 Weekly operating rhythm [REC]

- **One fixed weekly checkpoint** (day/time chosen by Tim) reviewing: what
  closed this week against the active milestone(s) in
  `06_MILESTONES.csv`, what is blocked and on whom, and whether any
  `slip_trigger` condition has been hit.
- **Bench/desk time protected in blocks**, not interleaved hour-by-hour ΓÇö
  the stage-40 burden estimates (┬º12.1) assume single-operator, serial
  bench work; context-switching between bench calibration and manuscript
  writing in the same day is a documented efficiency loss in that plan.
- **Advisor sync cadence:** at minimum, once per the gates in
  `06_ADVISOR_MEETING_BRIEF.md` (M02, M13, M28, M34) ΓÇö not necessarily
  weekly, but never less often than monthly during the AugΓÇôDec 2026
  bench-and-campaign-dense period.
- **Startup workstream check-in:** monthly, ~1 day, deliberately
  lightweight (M41/M43) so it never competes with critical-path time.

### 9.2 Measurable progress indicators [REC]

| Indicator | How measured | Where tracked |
|---|---|---|
| Milestones closed vs. planned | Count of `status=complete` rows in `06_MILESTONES.csv` vs. rows whose `target_date` has passed | Weekly checkpoint |
| Bench-days consumed vs. the ~19ΓÇô29 day Tier-1 estimate | Logged bench-days per session | Project 02 journal (existing practice) |
| Open gates | Count of unresolved I-/U-/G- gates from stage 40, and G-A..G-H from stage 50 | This roadmap's ┬º1 + `05_DISCLOSURE_HOLD_CHECKLIST.md` |
| Papers in each state (drafting / submitted / in review / accepted) | P1/P2/P3 status | `06_MILESTONES.csv` P1-MANUSCRIPT / WPD-ARCH / P3-MANUSCRIPT rows |
| Dissertation chapters drafted vs. 7 planned | Chapter count | M36/M37 |
| Committee/registration milestones met on schedule | M32/M33/M38/M39 dates vs. actual | Weekly checkpoint |
| Direction-gate conditions (G5, M34) | Binary: accepted/in-revision paper? real-die calibration achieved? | Advisor sync |

---

## 10. Cross-references

- Milestone-level detail, dates, dependencies, owners, and fallbacks for
  every item named above: [`06_MILESTONES.csv`](06_MILESTONES.csv).
- Advisor-facing summary of the decisions this roadmap assumes get made
  early (M01ΓÇôM03, M13, M28, M34): [`06_ADVISOR_MEETING_BRIEF.md`](06_ADVISOR_MEETING_BRIEF.md).
- Startup-preparation detail for the STARTUP workstream (M41ΓÇôM44):
  [`06_STARTUP_READINESS.md`](06_STARTUP_READINESS.md).
- This document deliberately does not re-derive the direction, venue
  route, experiment design, or IP screen ΓÇö it schedules them. Any
  disagreement between this roadmap's dates and the underlying technical
  content of stages 20/30/40/50 should be resolved in favor of those
  stages' technical content, with this document's dates adjusted
  accordingly.

55	own 2019 publications. The adjustment moves novelty to the *application +
56	calibrated measurement + architecture* level, adds four
57	campaign-uncoupled work packages (comparison table, multi-die
58	repeatability, calibration + uncertainty budget, hybrid Hall+inductive
59	fusion), and produces a **minimum-viable two-paper floor that does not

92	   SENSL-26-07-RL-1061), but only after the bench package above closes.

159	- Advisor decision batch #1 answered (┬º1 items 1ΓÇô7).
160	- UW e-mail sent (contingent on item 4).
